title: Will, going to, and plans
goal: Choose will, going to, or -ing for the future
intro: English has more than one future. “Will” is for decisions made now, promises and predictions. “Going to” is for plans you already decided and for things you can see coming. The present continuous is for arrangements with a time and a place. All three are correct; the difference is in how the speaker thinks.

rules.rule: will: a decision now, a promise, an offer, a prediction.
going to: a plan made before, or something you can see coming.
examples: I’m going to learn French this year.
Look at those clouds. It’s going to rain.
We’re flying to Goa on Friday.

mistakes.wrong: I will go to Shimla next week, we booked the tickets.
mistakes.right: I’m going to Shimla next week. We’ve booked the tickets.

mistakes.why: A decision at this moment: will.

mistakes.wrong: I will be going to office tomorrow.
mistakes.right: I’m going to the office tomorrow.
mistakes.why: Simple, natural plan: I’m going to the office.

ex.q: The phone is ringing. — I ___ get it.
ex.y: A decision now: I’ll get it.

ex.q: We ___ buy a new car next year. We’ve been saving for it.
ex.y: A plan made before: going to.
You can see it coming: going to.

ex.q: Don't worry, I am sending the file in five minutes.
ex.fixed: Don't worry, I will send the file in five minutes.

ex.q: She will reaches home by eight.
ex.fixed: She will reach home by eight.

ex.q: Tomorrow I go to the doctor at ten.
ex.fixed: Tomorrow I am going to the doctor at ten.

ex.q: It’s so hot. I think I ___ (have) a cold drink.

ex.a: I'm going to start running next month.
ex.y: A plan: going to + base form.

ex.q: Offer help with “will”: your friend’s bag is heavy.
ex.y: A quick offer: I’ll carry it / I’ll help you.

talk: Talk about your plans for next weekend and next year, and make two predictions about your city in ten years.
